Sexual Dysfunction

erectile disorder · desire and arousal · orgasm · sexual painOrganic or psychogenic, and what causes it?

1Script2Urgent3Differential4Workup5Criteria6Severity7Treatment8Follow-upPractice
1Illness script
Bottom line
  • Erections that also fail with masturbation, in sleep or on waking organic; erections kept there, failing only with a partner psychogenic, such as performance anxiety
  • Several causes in one history: ongoing heavy drinking points to alcohol; a drug started before the onset points to the drug; one taken for years before it, or a stable chronic disease, is less likely; a primary disorder needs 6 months or more and no drug, substance or medical cause
  • Remove the cause; psychogenic: sex therapy; organic: a phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitor first, never with a nitrate
What it is

Trouble with sexual desire, arousal (erectile dysfunction is the arousal disorder in men), orgasm, or pain with sex

Driver

Organic: damage to the nerves, blood supply or hormones of erection

Psychogenic: may stem from performance anxiety, stress or depression; may be tied to a partner or setting

Triggers

Heavy alcohol use, chronic or acute

Drugs: selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), antipsychotics, tricyclics, beta-blockers, spironolactone

Atherosclerosis, smoking and diabetes

Low testosterone or high prolactin

Performance anxiety, stress or depression

Chain

Organic: nerve, vessel or hormone injury erections fail in every setting, sleep included; at first now and then, later persistent

Psychogenic: anxiety or guilt about sex sudden failure with a partner or in one setting; nocturnal and morning erections kept

Overlap: organic failure reactive anxiety that compounds it

Insights

Erections in sleep or with masturbation show the nerves and vessels work, so a failure confined to partnered sex is psychological

A side effect would not newly emerge after years on a drug: the suspect is the drug started just before the onset

Populationtap to open
AcquiredErectile dysfunction that starts after normal function often has both organic and psychological causes
Older menSlower erection and ejaculation with age
PostmenopausalRule out medical causes such as vaginal atrophy before a desire or arousal disorder
2Urgent risks
Heart diseaseNew vascular erectile dysfunction is often the first sign of cardiovascular disease

If a man has new erectile dysfunction from a vascular cause, choose an evaluation for undiagnosed cardiovascular disease.

NitratesA phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitor with a nitrate or an alpha blocker can cause hypotension or syncope

If a man takes a nitrate, choose no phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitor.

3Differential
Erectile failure: substance, drug and medical causes first, most tempting first
CauseFingerprintDecides it

Atherosclerosis or diabetesSmoker or diabetic; erections weaken over timeGradual, from weak erections to none; a stable disease rarely explains a recent change

Low libido; infertility; headache with prolactinomaMorning testosterone low, then prolactin and luteinizing hormone
A statinOn the medication listNot a known cause of erectile dysfunction

Pause point
Heavy daily drinker; erections fail with a new partner and with masturbation Offered as performance anxiety, guilt or an SSRI taken for years Fails with masturbation too; the SSRI long predates the onset → Alcohol
Erectile failure and breast enlargement on sertraline and risperidone Offered as sertraline or diabetic neuropathy Gynecomastia points to prolactin → Risperidone
5Diagnostic criteria
Defining criteria: sexual dysfunctions Groups – desire (male hypoactive sexual desire disorder, female sexual interest/arousal disorder), arousal (erectile disorder), orgasm (premature or delayed ejaculation, female orgasmic disorder), pain (genito-pelvic pain/penetration disorder: vaginismus, dyspareunia) · Clock – 6 months or more · Exclusion – not from a drug, a substance or a medical condition · Premature ejaculation – within 1 minute of penetration; a normal time with masturbation does not rule it out
7Treatment
Treat the cause first
CauseChooseWatch for
AlcoholAbstinence or cutting downErections can improve
A drug started before the onsetStop or replace it
Diabetes, prolactinoma or low testosteroneTreat the disorderTestosterone alone rarely restores erections

Erectile dysfunction

1

First line, psychogenicErections kept in sleep, on waking or with masturbation

Sex therapy

The mainstay for psychogenic erectile dysfunction; works best started promptly

2

First line, organicErections fail in every setting; the cause removed or not reversible

A phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitor

Slows breakdown of cyclic guanosine monophosphate, so smooth muscle relaxes and blood fills the corpus cavernosum; contraindicated with nitrates or alpha blockers

3

Second lineA phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitor fails or is poorly tolerated

Vacuum device or penile injection

These may be used when the inhibitor fails or is poorly tolerated

Other disorders: first treatment
DisorderChooseWatch for
Premature ejaculationAn SSRIPuts the delayed ejaculation side effect to use
Pelvic floor physical therapyRule out a body cause first, in its brief

WhenDo or expect

Practice
  1. 27-year-old man with 3 months of lost erections with his new girlfriend began after a failed first attempt; dreads the next one wakes with erections; normal erections with masturbation desire intact; no drugs or alcohol; examination normal → Performance anxiety → erections kept on waking and with masturbation, failing only with a partner after a bad first attempt: psychogenic, performance anxiety; a vascular cause takes the sleep erections too, and desire here is intact
  2. 49-year-old man with 2 months of erectile failure erections also fail with masturbation; no morning erections drinks 8 beers nightly; sertraline for 9 years; worried his partner will leave examination and laboratory results normal → Alcohol use → erections fail with masturbation and on waking in a man who drinks heavily every day: alcohol; a drug taken for years would not newly cause it, and anxiety does not stop erections with masturbation
  3. 62-year-old man with 6 weeks of erectile failure and lower libido spironolactone added for heart failure 2 months ago type 2 diabetes well controlled for 12 years; no neuropathy no morning erections; drinks rarely → Spironolactone → erectile failure and low libido that began after spironolactone was started: the drug; diabetes stable for years is less likely to explain a recent change, and lost morning erections point away from anxiety
  4. 63-year-old man who smokes, with 1 year of worsening erections aching buttocks and thighs when walking, eased by rest no erections on waking; desire intact weak femoral and pedal pulses; both legs thin → Aortoiliac occlusion (Leriche syndrome) → erectile failure with buttock and thigh claudication and weak femoral pulses in a smoker: aortoiliac occlusion; lost waking erections point away from anxiety, and low testosterone would not explain claudication
  5. 58-year-old man with type 2 diabetes and 2 years of weakening erections none on waking or with masturbation; desire intact metformin only; no nitrates; does not drink morning testosterone normal; cardiac evaluation normal last month → Start a phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitor → gradual organic erectile dysfunction with diabetes, normal testosterone, no nitrate and a cardiac evaluation done: a phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitor first; testosterone alone rarely restores erections, and sex therapy is the mainstay only when erections are kept in sleep
  6. 31-year-old man with erectile failure since his divorce 2 months ago fails only with partners; normal erections on waking and with masturbation anxious before each encounter; libido intact no drugs or alcohol; examination normal → Sex therapy → sudden failure with partners only, with waking and masturbation erections kept: psychogenic, and sex therapy is the mainstay; prolactin and luteinizing hormone follow a low morning testosterone, and testosterone rarely restores erections
  7. 26-year-old man who ejaculates within a minute of penetration happens almost every time for the past year; distressed lasts longer with masturbation; erections firm no drugs or alcohol; examination normal → A selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor → ejaculation within 1 minute of penetration for 6 months or more: premature ejaculation, even with a normal time during masturbation; an SSRI treats it, a phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitor is for erectile failure, and bupropion lacks sexual side effects
  8. 54-year-old man with erectile failure for 6 weeks began 2 weeks after starting atenolol for hypertension erections also fail on waking and with masturbation drinks rarely; no diabetes; blood pressure now 128/80 mm Hg → Replace atenolol with another antihypertensive → erectile failure that began just after a beta-blocker was started: stop or replace the drug; a phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitor is typically tried as further therapy once the cause is addressed, and erections lost in sleep point away from a psychogenic cause
Pairs with SSRI Adverse Effects covers managing sexual dysfunction on an SSRI. Antipsychotic Adverse Effects covers prolactin rise from antipsychotics. Genito-Pelvic Pain/Penetration Disorder covers pain or fear with penetration.
Transferable rule

Ask where erections still work: kept in sleep, on waking or with masturbation means psychogenic; failing there too means organic, so line the causes up against the onset: ongoing heavy drinking, a drug started just before, then vascular or hormonal disease.
